record.paper_title: Methods for Computing All Roots of a Polynomial Simultaneously - Known Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Global convergence of the classical Weierstrass method
record.original_question: Given a monic polynomial f(x) of degree n with simple real or complex zeros, consider the classical Weierstrass simultaneous root-finding iteration started from a vector of distinct initial approximations in C^n. Is this iteration globally convergent outside a subset of the starting space of measure zero? More specifically, describe the exceptional set for n = 2, and determine whether the same measure-zero global-convergence statement holds for arbitrary n.

evidence.quote: "Show that the Weierstrass procedure is globally convergent outside of a set of measure zero in the starting space and describe this set, for n = 2. Show the same result, if possible for arbitrary n."

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let f(x) = x^n + a_{n-1}x^{n-1} + ... + a_0 be a monic polynomial of degree n ≥ 2 with complex coefficients and n pairwise distinct zeros ζ_1, ..., ζ_n ∈ C (the zeros may be real or complex). The classical Weierstrass (Durand–Kerner) simultaneous iteration is the map W: U → C^n defined on the open set U = { z = (z_1, ..., z_n) ∈ C^n : z_i ≠ z_j for i ≠ j } by

  W(z)_i = z_i − f(z_i) / ∏_{j ≠ i} (z_i − z_j),  i = 1, ..., n.

Starting from z^{(0)} ∈ U, set z^{(k+1)} = W(z^{(k)}) whenever z^{(k)} ∈ U. Say that the iteration converges (to the zeros of f) from z^{(0)} if z^{(k)} ∈ U for all k and there is a permutation σ of {1, ..., n} such that z^{(k)}_i → ζ_{σ(i)} as k → ∞ for every i.

(a) For n = 2, determine the set E_2 ⊂ C^2 of starting points z^{(0)} ∈ U from which the Weierstrass iteration fails to converge to (ζ_1, ζ_2) (in some order), and prove that E_2 has Lebesgue measure zero in C^2 ≅ R^4.

(b) For arbitrary n ≥ 2 and arbitrary monic f of degree n with simple zeros, decide whether the set E_n ⊂ C^n of starting points in U from which the Weierstrass iteration fails to converge to the zeros of f has Lebesgue measure zero in C^n ≅ R^{2n}; equivalently, decide whether the Weierstrass iteration is globally convergent outside a set of measure zero in the starting space.
artifact.status_search_result: A literature search indicates that global convergence of the classical Weierstrass (Durand–Kerner) iteration outside a measure-zero exceptional set remains an open problem. Existing results address only local/semilocal convergence under explicit initial conditions, modifications (SOR-Weierstrass, two-point variants), or restricted settings such as quaternionic polynomials; no proof of almost-everywhere global convergence for arbitrary n appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: General convergence theorems for iterative processes and applications to the Weierstrass root-finding method
status_evidence.snippet: Provides convergence theorems under initial conditions; does not establish global convergence outside a measure-zero set.
status_evidence.claim: Only semilocal convergence results are available; global a.e. convergence is not established.

status_evidence.title: Global Convergence Properties of the SOR-Weierstrass Method
status_evidence.snippet: Studies a modified (SOR) variant rather than proving a.e. global convergence of the classical Weierstrass iteration.
status_evidence.claim: Modifications of Weierstrass are studied because the global convergence question for the classical method is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Convergence of the Weierstrass Method for Simultaneous Approximation of Polynomial Zeros
status_evidence.snippet: Convergence theorems require explicit conditions on the initial approximations.
status_evidence.claim: No measure-theoretic global convergence statement is given for arbitrary n.
